source_text: Ceterum si, qua nouum deum praedicans, ueteris dei legem cupiebat excludere, quare de deo quidem nouo nihil praescribit, sed de uetere lege solummodo, nisi quoniam fide manente in creatorem sola lex eius concessare debebat? ut et psalmus ille praececinerat: disrumpam ua a nobis is uincula eorum et abiciamus eorum iugum a nobis; ex quo scilicet tumultuatae sunt gentes et populi meditati sunt inania, adstitel\'unt reges terrae et magi stratus conuenerunt in unum aduersus dominum et aduersus Christum eius. et utique, si alius deus praedicaretur a Paulo, nulla disceptatio esset seruandae legis necne, non pertinentis scilicet ad dominum nouum et aemulum legis. ipsa enim dei nouitas atque diuersitas abstulisset non modo quaestionem ueteris et alienae legis uerum omnem eius mentionem. sed hic erat totus status quaestionis, quid, cum idem deus legis in Christo praedicaretur, legi eius derogaretur. stabat igitur fides semper in creatore et Christo eius, sed conuersatio et disciplina nutabat. nam et alii de idolothyto edendo, alii de mulierum uelamento, alii de nuptiis uel repudiis, nonnulli et de spe resurrectionis disceptabant, de deo nemo. nam (si) fuisset haec quoque quaestio disceptata, et ipsa apud apostolum inueniretur, uel quanto principalis. quodsi post apostolorum tempora adulterium ueritas passa est circa dei regulam, ergo iam apostolica traditio nihil passa est in tempore suo circa dei regulam, et non alia agnoscenda erit traditio apostolorum quam quae hodie apud ipsorum ecclesias editur. nullam autem apostolici census ecclesiam inuenias, quae non in creatore christianizet. aut si hae erunt a primordio corruptae. quae erunt integrae? nimirum aduersariae creatoris. exhibe ergo aliquam ex tuis apostolici census, et obduxeris. igitur cum omnibus modis constet alium deum in regula sacramenti istius non fuisse a Christo usque ad Marcionem quam creatorem, satis iam et probatio nostra munita est, qua ostendimus notitiam dei haeretici ex euangelii et legis separatione coepisse, et definitio superior instructa est, non esse credendum deum, quem homo de suis sensibus composuerit, nisi plane prophetes. id est non de suis sensibus. quod si Marcion poterit dici, debebit etiam probari; ** nihil retractare oportebit. hoc enim cuneo ueritatis omnis extruditur haeresis, cum Christus non alterius dei quam creatoris circumlator ostenditur.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover, if, while preaching a new God, he desired to exclude the law of the old God, why does he prescribe nothing concerning the new God, but only concerning the old law, unless it is because faith remaining in the Creator, only His law should be conceded? So that also that Psalm had foretold: I will break their chains from us and cast off their yoke from us; from which, indeed, the nations were tumultuous and the peoples meditated on empty things, the kings of the earth stood and the rulers assembled together against the Lord and against His Christ. And certainly, if another God were being preached by Paul, there would be no dispute about keeping the law or not, not pertaining, of course, to the new Lord and rival of the law. For the very newness and diversity of the God would have removed not only the question of the old and foreign law, but all mention of it. But this was the whole state of the question, what, when the same God of the law was being preached in Christ, His law was being derogated. Therefore, faith always stood in the Creator and His Christ, but conversation and discipline were wavering. For others were disputing about eating idolothyton, others about the veiling of women, others about marriages or divorces, some also about the hope of resurrection, but no one about God. For if this question also had been disputed, it would also have been found with the apostle, or how much more important. But if, after the time of the apostles, the truth suffered adultery around the rule of God, then already the apostolic tradition suffered nothing in its time around the rule of God, and no other tradition of the apostles will be recognized than that which is published today in their churches. However, you will not find any church of apostolic census which does not Christianize in the Creator. Or if these are corrupted from the beginning, which ones will be intact? Doubtless, the ones opposed to the Creator. Therefore, show me some from your apostolic census, and you will be refuted. Therefore, since in all ways it is established that another God was not in the rule of this sacrament from Christ to Marcion than the Creator, our proof is already sufficiently fortified, by which we show that the knowledge of the heretic God began from the separation of the Gospel and the law, and the above definition is instructed, that one should not believe in a God whom a man has composed from his own senses, unless he is a prophet, that is, not from his own senses. Which if Marcion will be able to say, he will also have to prove; nothing will have to be retracted. For by this wedge of truth, all heresy is expelled, when Christ is shown to be the circumciser not of another God, but of the Creator.

choices.why: referring to the law of the Creator
emphasizing the importance of faith in the Creator

pass_b_english: If Marcion preaches a new God while trying to shut out the old God's law, why does he lay down not a single rule about this new deity, but only about the old law — unless it's because faith stayed put in the Creator, so that only the Creator's law could still be acknowledged? That very Psalm saw it coming: "Let us break their chains and throw off their yoke" (Psalm 2:3); and sure enough, the nations erupted, the peoples plotted emptiness, earth's kings took their stand, and rulers gathered as one against the Lord and against his Christ.

If Paul had been proclaiming a different God, there would have been zero debate over whether to keep the law — since that law wouldn't pertain to the new Lord and rival of the law in the first place. The sheer novelty and otherness of such a God would have erased not just the question of the old, alien law, but every mention of it. But that wasn't the issue. The whole dispute was this: when the very same God of the law is preached in Christ, why is his law being whittled away? Faith never budged from the Creator and his Christ; what wavered was conduct and discipline.

Some argued over eating idol-meat, some over women's veils, some over marriage or divorce, a few even over the hope of resurrection — but no one argued over God. If that question had been in play, it would have surfaced with the apostle, and how much more urgently. But if truth suffered adultery regarding God's rule after the apostles' time, then the apostolic tradition suffered no such corruption in its own day, and no other apostolic tradition will be recognized than the one published today in their churches.

You will not find a single church on the apostolic roll that does not Christianize in the Creator. And if those churches were corrupted from the start, which ones remain intact? Obviously, the ones opposed to the Creator. So produce one from your apostolic roll, and you'll be refuted. Since it's now established on every front that from Christ to Marcion no other God stood in the rule of this sacrament but the Creator, our proof stands fortified: we've shown the heretic's 'knowledge of God' began by severing Gospel from law, and the definition above holds — you must not believe in a God a man has cobbled together from his own senses, unless he's a prophet; that is, not from his own senses. If Marcion can claim that, he must prove it; nothing will be retracted. For by this wedge of truth all heresy is expelled, once Christ is shown to be the circumciser not of some other God, but of the Creator.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version. The scripture citation (Psalm 2:3) in Pass B correctly identifies the allusion in the Latin 'disrumpam ua a nobis is uincula eorum...' (Psalm 2:3). All clauses, including the complex conditional arguments regarding the apostolic tradition and the definition of a prophet, are preserved.
